title: Asia Among Most Vulnerable to AI Correction, Asean Unit Warns
key_facts: AMRO said in a report on Monday 5 Oct 2026 that Asia is "particularly exposed" to a possible AI correction
The Asean+3 region (South-east Asia plus China, Japan, South Korea) accounts for two-thirds of the growth in global AI-related trade
A slowdown in demand could cut up to 1.5 percentage points from 2027 growth, forecast at 4.1 per cent: the biggest risk factor named
A prolonged disruption in the Strait of Hormuz could cost 0.6 percentage point
South Korea's equity market is heavily concentrated in AI; Japan and Hong Kong move closely with US AI and tech assets
Lead economist Runchana Pongsaparn: "There are some warning signals, but we would say that they are not grave yet"
quote_evidence: Asia's powerhouse economies are more at risk than most from a potential artificial intelligence bust, which could undercut surging exports and send shockwaves across markets, a new study found.
"There are some warning signals, but we would say that they are not grave yet," its lead economist Runchana Pongsaparn said at a briefing on Monday.
why_it_matters_hint: Asia makes the chips and hardware for AI data centres, so a drop in AI spending would reach exports and markets there first.
notes: Bloomberg page blocked; text read in The Business Times (Singapore), which carries the Bloomberg report (BLOOMBERG credit at the end). Original: AMRO report published Monday 5 Oct 2026. Original Bloomberg link kept as url.
